title: Robert Baron: Philosophia theologiae ancillans (New English tip)

records.label: Section 1 — Only God is necessary being: real being divides into creator and creature
Section 2 — Only God is being by essence: existence is of the divine essence, not of the creature
Section 3 — God alone is pure act: real being divides into actual, potential, and mixed
Section 4 — Fourth division of real being: modes of existing — per se versus in another
Section 5 — Explanation of being, essence, existence, subsistence, suppositum, and person
Section 6 — Whether in creatures the suppositum and its singular nature really differ
Section 7 — Why philosophers attribute composition from essence and existence, and from essence and subsistence, to created substances but not to God
Section 8 — Given that every perfection is of God's essence, does personal subsistence follow; and is God, as communicable to three, a person (Cajetan)
Section 9 — Whether God, as common to the three persons, is a singular substance; and whether the three persons of the Trinity are three singular substances
Section 10 — Whether Christ, as man, is a person; and whether Christ, as man, is everywhere
Section 11 — Whether the Ubiquitarians' arguments drawn from the personal union are valid
Section 12 — Whether the personal subsistence of the Logos is communicated to his human nature; and whether they speak rightly who say Christ's humanity subsists everywhere by that subsistence
